title: Burp Suite — WSTG-Aligned Testing Hub
body: The OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG 4.2) organises web testing into 12 categories. Burp is the tool you run them with. This hub routes to a node per category — don't just open Burp and fuzz randomly; work the categories in order. INFO/CONF first (understand the surface), then auth (fastest wins), then input validation (the classic vulns), then the ones scanners can't do: authorization, session, and business logic. Client-side (CLNT), API (APIT), WebSocket, and Request Smuggling complete the picture — these are the categories that separate thorough testers from surface-level ones.
cmd:
# ══ OWASP WSTG 4.2 — 12 CATEGORIES, BURP IS YOUR TOOL ══════════════
# Work in this order. Every category has a node below.
#
# WSTG-INFO  Information Gathering        -> burp_recon
# WSTG-CONF  Config & Deployment          -> burp_recon
# WSTG-IDNT  Identity Management          -> burp_authn
# WSTG-ATHN  Authentication               -> burp_authn
# WSTG-ATHZ  Authorization                -> burp_authz
# WSTG-SESS  Session Management           -> burp_session
# WSTG-INPV  Input Validation             -> burp_input
# WSTG-ERRH  Error Handling               -> burp_input (error disclosure)
# WSTG-CRYP  Cryptography                 -> burp_session (TLS/token crypto)
# WSTG-BUSL  Business Logic               -> burp_logic
# WSTG-CLNT  Client-Side                  -> xss / burp_input
# WSTG-APIT  API Testing                  -> burp_input + burp_authz
#
# *** THE THREE SCANNERS CAN'T DO ***
# ATHZ / BUSL / IDNT — every request is valid, only context makes it abuse.
# A scanner can't reason that order #1043 belongs to another user, or that
# the password reset flow lets you skip email verification. That's you.
#
# SETUP: first visit? -> burp_setup

# QUICK RECON — map the surface before you start testing:
# Spider: Target -> right-click host -> Spider this host
# JS analysis: Target -> Site map -> find .js files -> Engagement Tools -> Find scripts
# Active scan (Pro): right-click -> Scan -> Audit
warn: Don't open Burp and immediately go to Intruder. Map the surface first (WSTG-INFO/CONF) — you need to know what endpoints exist before you test them. The three categories that find the most real bugs (ATHZ, BUSL, IDNT) are manual reasoning, not tool output. Burp surfaces the requests; you supply the logic.

choices.label: Setup — proxy, CA cert, scope, FoxyProxy
INFO/CONF — recon, spider, JS, tech fingerprint
ATHN/IDNT — auth bypass, mass assignment, brute
ATHZ — IDOR, priv escalation, access control
SESS — cookies, JWT, CSRF, session fixation
INPV — SQLi, XSS, SSRF, SSTI, XXE, CMDi
BUSL — business logic, race conditions, workflow
CLNT — DOM XSS, clickjacking, postMessage, prototype pollution
APIT — REST API, GraphQL, BOLA, mass assignment
Request smuggling — CL.TE / TE.CL / H2.TE desync
